A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoV and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite the revised title, substantial reformatting and relocation of results.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, retrieval comparisons, prompt-pool experiments, transfer results and repeated-seed measurements, including in its appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original evaluations and adds ranking comparisons, component ablations, computational measurements and training-data diagnostics.

M1.justification: The proposed AutoV procedure remains unchanged: frozen feature extraction, first-layer modality interaction, mapping networks, pairwise reward supervision, cosine-distance pre-filtering and highest-score selection. Regression and list-wise ranking are added experimental alternatives rather than replacements for the proposed method.

E1.justification: V3 narrows reported benchmark coverage from fifteen to fourteen and removes POPE results from Table 1, although Appendix B still describes POPE. Other benchmark and training datasets are retained; v3 Table 2 matches v2 appendix Table 5. V3 also adds a query-only diagnostic on existing training data.

E2.justification: V3 Table 3 adds absolute-loss regression and list-wise ranking to the retrieval comparison previously reported in v2 Table 2. Fixed prompts, random selection, MoE and pairwise AutoV remain. The principal benchmark comparators—FGVP, Circle and API—are unchanged.

E3.justification: Several new evaluation protocols vary decoder layers, pre-filtering with six or eight candidates, strategy-teacher sizes of 0.5B and 4B, and pool size, model size and visual-token count for computational measurements. Appendix D introduces query-only and GPT-4o-judged filtering diagnostics. These substantially extend experimental controls without establishing changes to the retained experiments' training settings.

E4.justification: V3 adds substantial analyses of ranking objectives, layer selection, inference pre-filtering, computational scaling, language-prior filtering and teacher scale. These test previously unexamined design choices and assumptions. Conversely, v2's ten-case appendix retrieval gallery is omitted, although two examples reappear in v3 Figure 1.

E5.justification: The paired t-test reporting and five MMMU runs with seeds 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 are unchanged. V2 Appendix E/Table 6 becomes v3 Appendix F/Table 9, retaining the same reported mean, standard deviation and p-value threshold. No additional uncertainty-reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial results for the new comparisons and analyses, including regression/list-wise average scores of 39.6/40.6 and query-only accuracy falling from 32.7% to 13.2% after filtering. Shared benchmark cells, closed-source results and prompt-pool scores remain unchanged. POPE entries are removed; revised cross-benchmark averages cover seven rather than eight tasks and do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), including feature extraction, scoring, pairwise reward loss and attention-prompt construction, are retained. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs, and the new analyses are empirical.

C1.justification: The central retrieval and automatic loss-ranking contributions remain intact. V3 adds prompt-engineering saturation and difficult human prompt annotation to its central motivation, and strengthens the conclusion to claim that effectiveness does not depend on individual prompts' intrinsic quality. The headline benchmark gains are retained.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations linking regression weakness to noisy absolute losses and list-wise weakness to optimization complexity. It interprets filtering diagnostics as stronger visual grounding and discusses teacher-scale efficiency tradeoffs. The practical pool-size recommendation changes from fewer than seven to fewer than nine candidates; v2's MoE-overfitting explanation is removed.

D1.justification: V3 Appendix C specifies the loss-annotation model as LLaVA-v1.5 7B and estimates the annotation workload at half a day on one A100-40G. Section 5.8 supplies token counts and component-level computational accounting. Existing training epochs, batch size, learning rate and training hardware remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds the original Gemini technical report and removes VisionZip and SparseVLM references. Related work places greater emphasis on diminishing returns from prompt engineering and complementary prompt retrieval. Most cited work and the distinction from external retrieval-augmented methods are retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, retrieval-comparison discussion, efficiency discussion and conclusion are substantially revised. Analysis becomes a separate main section, related work receives numbered subsections, and the appendices are reorganized. This exceeds simple renumbering or prose added solely for new experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, extensively restyles tables and redraws Figure 1 as a two-panel motivation figure. Extended benchmark results move from the appendix to main Table 2, new analysis tables are added, and the appendix retrieval gallery is removed. Table 1 drops POPE and average columns.

improvement.justification: The new ranking comparisons, component ablations and language-prior diagnostics give the unchanged method better empirical justification, while annotation-cost details improve transparency. The net gain is limited by removal of POPE evaluation and incomplete consistency checks: Appendix B still lists POPE, and the retained five-seed gains average 2.46 points although the statistical summary reports 2.06.
